_status: CLAIM MANIFEST ONLY. Nothing in this file is evidence. Every entry names the EXTERNAL authority that establishes it and the method by which the Move 85 gate must check it. The gate compares this file AGAINST those authorities; it must never compare an authority against this file, and it must never treat a value here as established because this file contains it.

_baseline.authority: REAL_MOVE84, supplied externally at adoption time
_baseline.how_verified: recompute the SHA-256 of the externally supplied artifact and compare with the externally pinned expected value held in the gate; this file's copy is checked against that result, never the reverse

_status_vocabulary.historically_established: established by adopted evidence in an earlier move; Move 85 does not re-establish it
_status_vocabulary.freshly_reproduced_by_move_85: measured again by this move's own gate run
_status_vocabulary.established_android_termux_aarch64_only: measured, and only on that platform
_status_vocabulary.source_level_contract: a structural property of the adopted source, machine-checkable from adopted bytes; NOT a runtime or reachability proof
_status_vocabulary.known_limitation: a real limit of the system, deliberately preserved and visible
_status_vocabulary.unestablished: not established by any evidence this project holds

claims.statement: The adopted Rust source defines exactly two verdict constants, VERDICT_FAIL and VERDICT_INCONCLUSIVE. No PASS verdict constant exists.
claims.authority: adopted rust/witness-verify/src/main.rs bytes
claims.how_verified: enumerate `const VERDICT_*` declarations from the adopted source and require the set to be exactly {VERDICT_FAIL, VERDICT_INCONCLUSIVE}
claims.does_not_establish: This is a structural fact about declared constants. It is NOT a proof that no reachable PASS-producing path exists anywhere in the program. No such global reachability proof is claimed.

claims.statement: No Rust PASS verdict was observed across the adopted tested corpus and the Move 85 audit-pack surfaces.
claims.authority: fresh execution of the freshly built verifier over every audit-pack case
claims.how_verified: capture every Rust stdout in the pack and require that none carries a PASS verdict and that no Rust invocation exits 0
claims.does_not_establish: Finite execution establishes what was observed on the tested surfaces only. It does not establish global reachability.

claims.statement: A clean bundle yields Rust INCONCLUSIVE with exit code 3.
claims.authority: fresh execution over the frozen reference bundle
claims.how_verified: run the freshly built verifier and compare against the adopted Move 84 authority binary built from the externally supplied adopted archive

claims.statement: A clean bundle yields Python PASS with exit code 0.
claims.authority: fresh execution of the adopted companion CLI
claims.how_verified: run it and record the exact bytes and exit code

claims.statement: A single-byte tamper to a top-level declared file is detected by the Rust verifier, which reports FAIL with exit code 1.
claims.authority: fresh execution; the reason code is read from that execution and never predicted
claims.how_verified: run the verifier over the tampered fixture and record the reason code observed

claims.statement: A single-byte tamper to the nested evidence payload is NOT detected by the Rust verifier. Its output is byte-identical to the clean bundle.
claims.authority: fresh execution, plus the adopted Move 80 case M80-CHANGED-EVIDENCE-001
claims.how_verified: require the Rust output for this case to be byte-identical to the clean case; the gate FAILS if the blindness is not observed, so the limitation cannot silently disappear

claims.statement: The same nested tamper IS detected by the Python lane, which fails at its nested-checksum stage.
claims.authority: fresh execution of the adopted companion CLI
claims.how_verified: require a non-zero exit and an error naming the nested evidence file

claims.statement: Exactly two adopted behavioural divergence IDs remain: stage_manifest_json_invalid and stage_report_field_missing_repaired.
claims.authority: the adopted Move 79 gate bytes, tools/check_move79_instrument_adoption.sh, which exports EXPECT_DIV_IDS
claims.how_verified: parse EXPECT_DIV_IDS out of the adopted gate at run time and require this file's list to equal it exactly; the adopted gate is the authority and this list is never the authority

claims.statement: The generic system-agreement markers remain visible and are not concealed.
claims.authority: the Move 84 child gate's own retained output
claims.how_verified: require SYSTEM_AGREEMENT_RESULT: FAIL and SYSTEM_AGREEMENT_REASON: BEHAVIOURAL_DIVERGENCE_DETECTED in the child transcript

claims.statement: Python and Rust are behaviourally equivalent.
claims.authority: none
claims.how_verified: not applicable; the two divergences above are preserved precisely because this is false

claims.statement: The verifier reports the version string 0.0.8-step79-diagnostics, which is distinct from the Cargo package version 0.0.8.
claims.authority: the freshly built binary's own output
claims.how_verified: parse the version from real output using the adopted reader; the Cargo version is read from the adopted manifest bytes
